0.0.n: A formal word for 今日, suited to an official announcement.

0.1.n: Marks the starting point in time, more formally than から.

0.2.n: The family name in 孫易磊, the pitcher's full name.

0.3.n: The first character of 易磊, the pitcher's given name; it is not a separate word here.

0.4.n: The second character of 易磊, the pitcher's given name; it is not a separate word here.

0.5.n: Placed after the player's name to identify his baseball position.

0.7.n: In Japanese professional baseball, this status makes a player eligible for first-team selection, unlike developmental status.

0.8.n: 登録する becomes passive 登録される, then polite past 登録されました, showing the player received the registration.

0.10.n: With お願いします, this asks listeners to welcome and support the player.

0.11.n: A polite request expression completing よろしくお願いします; the announcer asks for goodwill toward the player.

1.0.n: 皆 with the respectful ending さん politely addresses the whole group.

1.2.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

2.0.n: The group returns the same daytime greeting enthusiastically.

3.0.n: The everyday word for the current day, less formal than 本日.

3.1.n: Marks 今日 as the starting time for joining the team.

3.2.n: The polite form of 合流する, describing joining a group; the team is understood from context.

4.0.n: Sets the starting point for the speaker's ongoing relationship with the team.

4.1.n: With お願いします, this expresses hope for a good relationship rather than a specific favor.

4.2.n: Completes the polite set phrase よろしくお願いします, commonly used when introducing yourself to new teammates or colleagues.

0.lit: Today from, pitcher Sun Yi-Lei was registered under official roster status. Favorably, I ask!
0.tip: 支配下登録 means official roster registration, not automatic placement on the active first-team roster.

1.tip: 皆さん is a friendly, polite way to address a group.

2.tip: こんにちは can be returned unchanged when someone greets you.

3.lit: Today from, I will join the group.
3.tip: Japanese often leaves out I and the team when context makes them clear.

4.lit: From now on, favorably, I ask!
4.tip: よろしくお願いします is a set expression for requesting goodwill when beginning a relationship, not a literal request for something specific.
